name: Geraldine Quintero
life: “I still remember hiding a love letter in a leather case.” Thursday often includes a stop at Harbour Bakery, where Geraldine buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I got my old glasses back and finally read the note I found in their case.
appearance: Geraldine has a gray streak running back from the forehead, a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. When somebody else has the floor, Geraldine looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Geraldine takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To return the old note to its addressee.
family: Nora Reiss is Geraldine’s cousin’s child. Geraldine is free to hang up first. Nora makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The thirteenth doughnut*, Nora says, “The bank wants a sales forecast for the spare slot.”
connections: Jody Mehta. The temple repair identifies the frame and the note in its case.

reactions.situation: The witness asks to read the page alone
reactions.response: Geraldine finds a quiet place for the witness and waits without reading over a shoulder.

reactions.response: Geraldine offers the shortfall once and accepts the answer, including a refusal.

reactions.situation: When a relative dismisses a little luxury
reactions.response: Geraldine asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
